article.Citation: Brown TK, Alper K. Treatment of opioid use disorder with ibogaine: detoxification and drug use outcomes. The American Journal of Drug and Alcohol Abuse. 2018.
article.Title: Treatment of opioid use disorder with ibogaine: detoxification and drug use outcomes

article.IsObservational: Methods explicitly state 'this observational study' assesses outcomes 'without modifying the independent variable' and that 'investigators had no role in administering ibogaine or clinical management'; treatment was delivered as usual care by independent private clinics on a fee-for-service basis, not per a research-controlled protocol, and there is no randomization or comparator arm. Coded Y.
article.Substance: Primary substance is ibogaine HCl (mean total dose 1,540 ± 920 mg). Five of the 30 subjects additionally received a crude extract of T. iboga root bark (mean dose 1610 ± 1650 mg) alongside ibogaine HCl. Coded Substance as 'Ibogaine' since this is the extraction/treatment for the entire sample; the co-administered crude extract in a subset is noted here rather than as a separate substance value.
article.N: Analyzed sample is N=30 (all enrolled subjects). Follow-up n available declined over time (20, 19, 14, 17, 14 at 1/3/6/9/12 months respectively; SOWS returned on 27), but the primary statistical analyses (paired t-tests) used the full enrolled N=30 with missing follow-up values imputed to pretreatment baseline, so N=30 was used as the article's stated analyzed sample size.
article.AE_denominator: The 'Adverse events' section states 'No clinically significant cardiovascular or other medical events occurred in this study' without giving an explicit numbered safety population. All 30 enrolled subjects underwent the same monitored ibogaine treatment protocol (continuous pulse oximetry, 3-lead EKG, BP monitoring, ACLS-certified staff present) described in Methods, so the AE statement is inferred to cover the full enrolled cohort; denominator coded as 30.
article.PctBIPOC: Table 1 Ethnicity: 27 Caucasian, 1 Hispanic, 2 other (N=30). BIPOC computed as non-Caucasian = 1 Hispanic + 2 other = 3/30 = 10.0%. Note the table's use of 'Hispanic' as a distinct category from 'Caucasian' is the study's own classification scheme (not standard US Census race/ethnicity separation); treated as non-white per the codebook definition.
article.PctIndigenous: Not separately reported. Table 1 lists only 'Caucasian', 'Hispanic', and '2 other' for ethnicity with no further breakdown of the 'other' category, so Indigenous status cannot be determined.
article.AnyAEReported: The dedicated 'Adverse events' subsection under Results states in full: 'No clinically significant cardiovascular or other medical events occurred in this study.' This is the article's own explicit safety-reporting statement, so AnyAEReported is coded N with NumDistinctAEs=0, NParticipantsWithAE=0, and WorstSeverity='None'. Note the qualifier 'clinically significant' — the article does not report common/minor expected effects (e.g., transient nausea, ataxia) with counts, only this global null statement, so more granular minor AEs may be underreported by the source article itself rather than by this extraction. The Discussion's mention of ibogaine's association with cardiac fatalities and arrhythmia is background literature about ibogaine generally (citing other studies), not an AE observed in this study's cohort, and was not counted here.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Set to 0 for internal consistency with NumDistinctAEs=0 and AnyAEReported='N'; the article does not report this figure directly since it states no AEs occurred.
